artifacts.title: Dudt v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: RE Dudt was convicted and suspended from office by the Midway Presbyterian Church Session for emailing the congregation an SJC decision and expressing disagreement with a Session action, which the Session characterized as violating his ordination vows. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversing in whole and rendering a verdict of not guilty, finding that the Session had no constitutional authority to forbid Dudt from distributing the SJC decision and that the charges of false statements were not proven. A concurring opinion by several judges cautioned against elders emailing congregations in disagreement with Session decisions.

artifacts.title: Marusich v. Central Indiana Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC remanded the case to Central Indiana Presbytery with instructions to appoint a committee to reinvestigate under BCO 31-2, after its non-judicial commission declined to find a strong presumption of guilt against an accused teaching elder. The dissent argued the SJC failed to give proper great deference under BCO 39-3.3 to the presbytery's investigative commission's discretionary judgment declining to indict, and that the BCO does not require the investigative procedures ordered by the Decision.

artifacts.title: Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery

The case generated a concurring opinion offering procedural guidance on BCO 31-2 investigations versus BCO 32-2 charges, and a dissenting opinion by RE Haigler arguing the record showed unambiguous heterodoxy warranting a finding of strong presumption of guilt.

artifacts.title: Fitzsimmons v. Evangel
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission found that Evangel Presbytery erred in failing to notify appellant E.L. Fitzsimmons of the time and place of the hearing on his appeal and in failing to adjudicate the appeal once it was found to be in order. The case was remanded to Evangel Presbytery for proper rehearing and adjudication in accordance with BCO 42-8.

artifacts.title: Fitzsimmons v. Evangel Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained an appeal by E. L. Fitzsimmons against Evangel Presbytery's handling of his appeal from excommunication. The court found that Presbytery erred by failing to notify the appellant of the time, date, and place for hearing the appeal and by rescinding its earlier finding that the appeal was in order, thus failing to adjudicate the appeal properly. The case was remanded to Evangel Presbytery for proper adjudication on the merits.

artifacts.title: Nickoley v. Rocky Mountain
artifacts.synopsis: Rocky Mountain Presbytery erred in immediately deposing Rev. Bruce Nickoley for contumacy without giving him reasonable opportunity to defend himself under the due process provisions of the Book of Church Order. The case was remanded to the presbytery with recommendations to either institute a formal prosecution with due process or revoke the deposition and reinstate Nickoley.

artifacts.synopsis: Conrad and others challenged Central Carolina Presbytery's refusal to institute process against TE Stephen Stout and to permit them to act as voluntary prosecutors. The SJC denied both claims, holding that the presbytery properly found no strong presumption of guilt and retained authority over voluntary prosecution under BCO 31-1 through 31-3.

artifacts.title: Parks et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Parks and others challenged Northside Session's plan for multiple elder resignations, pastor severance, a delayed pastoral call, and bylaw revisions. The SJC denied every specification, holding that the plan did not violate BCO 24-6, 20-6, 20-2, or 25-7; a dissent was recorded.
